title: Cubic, Reciprocal & Exponential Graphs

problems_fixed.what: Within-tier duplicate answer: y=2^x at x=3 gives 8, colliding with bronze[0] (y=x^3 at x=2 -> 8), literally the same product 2x2x2. Changed x=3 to x=4 so y=16, distinct and still teaching powers of 2.
problems_fixed.old: For y=2^x, find y when x=3 (solution 8)
problems_fixed.new: For y=2^x, find y when x=4 (solution 16)

solutions_audit: Fresh-solved all 20 bank problems (8 bronze / 7 silver / 5 gold) from display text. Every stored solution was already mathematically correct (cubes incl. negatives, reciprocals with sign, powers, 2^-3 = 1/8, the population initial value 500x1.05^0 = 500, and a = -8 from the point (4,-2)). The only defect was one within-tier duplicate-answer collision in bronze (a filed disease class on these boards). No wrong answers, no degenerate or non-calculator-messy problems.

reordering.what: Moved the two multiple_choice problems (graph type, graph shape) to the end so all single_value problems precede them. Reason 1: the validator's within-tier duplicate check shares one numeric space for MC option-indices and real answers; MC index 2 (b2 'reciprocal') collided with the real answer 2 (y=6/x at x=3). Putting reals first (all distinct) with MCs exempt removes the false collision without altering any numbers. Reason 2: keeps a walkable single_value problem (y=x^3 at x=2) first so the player's auto-dealt completion problem works.

Reordered so the four single_value problems precede the three multiple_choice ones. The original silver[0] was multiple_choice, which the player cannot deal half-worked as the completion problem; now y=x^3-8 (-> 0) leads. No numbers changed.

misconceptions: Every misconception rebuilt to pattern/message/expect/note. The board's originals had no expect key (would fail the validator) and several carried em dashes. Each single_value misconception now carries a derived, error-committing expect that differs from the correct answer: e.g. 2x3=6 for a cube, +8 for a dropped sign on (-2)^3, 0.5 for a flipped reciprocal 3/6, 30 for 5x2x3 vs 5x2^3, 27 for a forgotten minus on -x^3, 26 for cubing before the bracket in (x-1)^3, 525 for 500x1.05 (adding an unearned year), 1/6 for 2^-3 read as 1/(2x3), and -0.5 for dividing instead of multiplying to find a. Multiple_choice misconceptions use expect:null.

guided_added.tier_descriptions: Rewrote bronze/silver/gold_description one-liners for the three graph families.
guided_added.tier_guides: bronze/silver/gold reference cards, each a stepped example landing on an answer step, all within the 115-word budget.
guided_added.opener: Bacteria doubling every hour (1,2,4,8,...) with an inline theme-safe SVG exponential curve plotting (0,1),(1,2),(2,4),(3,8),(4,16),(5,32); 2 read-off boxes (16 after 4 h, 32 after 5 h) then a reveal naming the exponential y=2^x and introducing the cubic (x^3) and reciprocal (a/x) families.

teach_walks.bronze: reciprocal y=8/x at x=2 and x=-4 plus branch/asymptote facts (2 branches, 0 axes touched)
teach_walks.silver: exponential y=4^x at x=2,0,-1 (incl 4^-1=0.25) and the shared (0,1) property
teach_walks.gold: horizontal asymptote of y=1/x+3 by watching 1/x shrink to 0 as x grows, landing on y=3

guided_added.guided_steps: Added to all 14 non-multiple-choice bank problems; each has a phase:substitute completion boundary (>=1 box before, >=2 live boxes after) and a final verifying check step. The 5 multiple_choice problems keep no walk (permitted).
guided_added.hints: One plain-text hint per problem pointing at the method move.

method_card_trimmed: Slimmed to 4 steps with content under the 140-word budget; example uses y=6/x table of values.
worked_examples_fix: Preserved all three worked examples, but changed em-dash step labels ('Step 1 - Substitute', 'Step 1 - Vertical asymptote', 'Step 2 - Horizontal asymptote', 'Step 1 - Growth or decay', 'Step 2 - Calculate') to colons, per the hard no-em-dash style rule (validator scans these strings).
opener_concept: Bacteria doubling every hour from 1: the student continues the doubling by common sense (16 after 4 h, 32 after 5 h); the reveal names it as the exponential curve y=2^x through (0,1), then introduces the cubic and reciprocal families the lesson covers.
